title: Do you guys use multi agents to work on your game projects?
author: Beginning-Sign1916
selftext: Just curious on this part and if anyone of you are using multi agents feel free to share I would love to know more about your approach and what’s the pros and cons to it

comments.author: HEXAPONG
comments.body: You decide how many agents to use? Anytime I do anything there are 3+ agents working.

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body: Just 3? Don't you need 6 to play hexapong?

replies.author: MrDankyStanky
replies.body: At least with Claude I think it's tied to model effort.

replies.author: Elegant_Tech
replies.body: If you need to save compute you can ask it to work through the plan assigning agents in serial so it only uses one at a time. This gives the benefit of having a lead agent that double checks the others work catching issues and sending it back for fixing or adding it to a later step.

comments.author: orbital_trace
comments.body: I do use multi agents. Usually front end, backend, beta tester, performance optimizer. And I just let them rip on high level tasks heres a video [https://www.loom.com/share/f2c52e824b1f41a8a18000a2df67adf8](https://www.loom.com/share/f2c52e824b1f41a8a18000a2df67adf8)

comments.author: dilberry
comments.body: I have Claude world building/handling graphical design, and constructing handoffs to Codex for Astra to complete where it is more competent. When Codex finishes, Claude takes the files by itself and implements them. I then prompt it for more tasks for Codex, which I give to Codex to do via my dot.

comments.author: Bulky_Blood_7362
comments.body:
Yea.
I have an orchestrator who send threads, ask me for visual/audio feedback, review the work, etc.

comments.author: Ok-Foundation-8006
comments.body: I have 17 agents that own a specific development role in my game. It’s expensive but the quality and accuracy make it worth it.

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body: Every agent has it's strengths. I use at least 4 most of the time. One for drafting, one for blueprinting, one for architecture/construction and one for art is the usual 'basic loadout' with various agents for sub tasks and edge cases.

comments.author: Legitimate-Paint2165
comments.body:
Claude orchestrates Codex, GLM, and Ollama.

Claude can impersonate entities that care about different things.

replies.author: Limp_Bus3865
replies.body: why would you use codex for anything when tou have claude

comments.author: brawnyai_redux
comments.body:
It depends on the stage. Initial phase where we are building the basic gameplay and if it's not MMO or things like that, I use ChatGPT 6 Pro to scope and create the plan. 

Then I can have Fable or Astra to become the orchestrator and the mastermind. Then I assign 3 agents like Sol or Opus to work under them. 

As things go, I direct a smarter AI to troubleshoot or scope and others to execute, to save tokens basically. Also having multiple agents working makes things less prone to errors.

comments.author: Such--Balance
comments.body:
Sometimes, but to me and my smallish project it doesnt really add any value. The limiting factor is my weekly usage limits anyway. Doing singular tasks actually uses less usage than doing multi agent tasks overall.

Yes, you could work faster with multi agents. But if that means hitting your limit on day 3 and then having to wait 4 more days..whats the added value?
